units.text: INT. PARLOUR - SPEKE HOUSE - DAY - 1894
Shuttered.
Sheets thrown over the furniture like drowned ghosts.
A single shaft of light picks out a brass phonograph on a side table, its horn pointing at the door.
No one.
The clock on the mantel has stopped at twenty past four.
The front door opens somewhere in the house.
Footsteps.
They cross a hall.
Slow, then slower.
A WOMAN steps into the parlour.
EVELINE ASHCROFT (40s, black mourning silk, travelling veil thrown back, face closed like a locked drawer).
She holds a leather satchel against her chest.
She stands in the light and doesn't take it in.
Her eyes go to the sheets, the clock.
Then to the phonograph.
She crosses and lifts the dust cloth from it.
Beneath, a wax cylinder sits on the spindle, labelled in a young hand: For E. — Michaelmas.
She sets down the satchel.
Wipes her glove across the horn and winds the crank.
Twelve turns.
She sets the needle.
A hiss, then a crackle.
Then a voice, warm and bright, drifting in from a decade ago.
Is it recording? Is it? Oh, Papa, say something to it.
units.name: EVELINE

units.text: A pause on the cylinder.
Eveline is frozen, one hand on the horn.
Very well, I shall say something. I shall say that I am eighteen, and the house is mine for the summer, and I shall never, ever leave it.
units.name: EVELINE

units.text: The recording hisses and breaks into laughter.
Real Eveline's mouth moves, almost a smile, almost not.
She takes the glove off, finger by finger.
Touches the horn with her bare palm.
Liar.
units.name: EVELINE

units.text: She lifts the needle.
The room goes silent.
She sits on a sheeted chair, and the dust stirs up around her in the light like smoke.
She doesn't weep.
She looks at the clock.
She stands and crosses to it, opens the glass, and with one finger, restarts the pendulum.
It ticks.
FADE OUT.
